finding: The one screen where the external client actually decides is not designed: the centre of the board is a white rectangle containing the literal string "(the site, page tabs, and Your notes)". The client is half of this product's user base and this is their only working screen.
evidence: Screenshot of 1339:7171 at 1280x720 — a 220x100 white box on an empty page, header + footer only. Its text nodes are: '{Agency}', 'is asking for your feedback', '(the site, page tabs, and Your notes)', 'Signed as {Name}…' (x2), 'Request changes', 'Approve this design', cookie line. Code implements all of it: page tabs review-client.tsx:52-66, sandboxed snapshot iframe :67-72, 'What's new' changeSummary block :309-314, 320px notes sidebar :322-369.
recommend: Draw the real two-column screen — page tabs, the frozen snapshot pane, the What's-new block, the notes rail — and treat it as the module's archetype. Every other Client sign-off board is a state of this one.

finding: A and B are two mutually incompatible partial drawings of the SAME code branch. A draws the verdict footer but a placeholder body; B draws the notes rail and the two-column body but has no footer at all — so read literally, B is a state where the client cannot approve or request changes.
evidence: review-client.tsx:280-463 is one branch covering both; the only difference is the local `asking` modal state. Board B (1340:7162) text nodes: '{Agency}', 'Your notes', a posted note, 'Anything you'd like changed?', 'Add note' — no 'Request changes', no 'Approve this design', no 'Signed as', and no header subtitle. Board A has the footer but an empty body. Screenshotted both.
recommend: Merge into one archetype board with a posted-note variant. 'Has commented' is a content state of the notes rail, not a screen.

finding: The single irreversible action in the whole agency product — closing a review round — has a purpose-built confirm modal in code with THREE copy variants and its own error state, and zero boards anywhere in the file.
evidence: review-client.tsx:375-463. Variants: approve ('This tells your designer the design is settled and they can put it live'), request-changes-with-note ('Your note below is sent with this… This closes the round and you cannot reopen it'), request-changes-without-note ('Your designer will not be told what to change, because you have not written a note'). Plus an in-dialog failure line :392-397 ('Your note could not be sent, so nothing was submitted'). Buttons differ per branch: 'Not yet' vs 'Go back'. Search of all 341 product frames for a client confirm board returns nothing.
recommend: Board all three copy variants plus the note-failed state. This is where sign-off is actually given and it is the least designed moment in the module.

finding: Client sign-off's zero outbound edges are CORRECT, not a gap — the code makes the client terminal on purpose. The real gap is the other user: nothing tells the agency the client acted. This refines D-X-02, which asked where a client should land.
evidence: review-client.tsx:246-249 comment: 'D · approved, and E · approved but edited since. Both are terminal for the client'. The `data.status !== "PENDING"` branch (:250-275) renders heading + one paragraph + 'Signed as', zero controls, and the preview iframe is gone. Meanwhile grep for createNotification in server/services/review.service.ts and client-review.service.ts returns NO match — the whole review loop notifies by email only, and notifyReviewSubmitted (review.service.ts:568) filters the requester out of the recipient list.
recommend: Do not wire client-side outbound edges. Instead label 1339:7186 'TERMINAL by design' the way 1339:7193 already is, and open the real gap as an agency-side one (see D-D-14, D-D-15, D-D-17).

screen: Client sign-off · D · approved + C · changes-requested
finding: The header subtitle contradicts the body on the terminal screens: the board says '{Agency} is asking for your feedback' directly above 'You approved this'. The agency is not asking for feedback any more — the client already gave it. This is a live product defect, not a file-only nit, and the three terminal boards do not even agree with each other about it.
evidence: Shell renders the subtitle unconditionally — review-client.tsx:89-92, `is asking for your feedback` inside the header, and every state passes through ``. Boards 1339:7186 (D) and 1339:7193 (C) both carry the subtitle; board 1340:7174 (E) does not. So 2 of 3 terminal boards mirror the code bug and the third silently fixes it.
recommend: Make the subtitle state-dependent in Shell — 'is asking for your feedback' while PENDING, and the agency name alone once resolved — then redraw all three terminal boards consistently.

finding: Boards D and C omit the 'Signed as {Name} · {email}' line that the code renders on every non-PENDING state, while board E draws it. 1339:7193's own frame name asserts the branch 'renders text + Signed as' — the name is right and the board is not.
evidence: review-client.tsx:272-274 places the Signed-as paragraph OUTSIDE the approved/changes ternary, so it renders for both. Text dump: 1339:7186 = '{Agency} · is asking for your feedback · You approved this · Thanks — {Agency} can take it from here…' (no Signed as); 1339:7193 likewise; 1340:7174 = '… · Signed as {Name} · {email}'.
recommend: Add the Signed-as line to 1339:7186 and 1339:7193. It is the client's only receipt that the approval is attributed to them.

finding: The cookie banner is drawn only on A · viewing, but it is mounted globally, so it also covers A0 · identify — the screen where the client is asked for their name and email. Consent competing with the collection of personal data is exactly the state worth boarding, and it is the one state not boarded.
evidence: CookieConsent is rendered in app/layout.tsx:69 via GlobalProviders (components/global/global-providers.tsx:11), so it is on every route including /review/[token]. Board 1339:7171 carries 'We use cookies to improve your experience.'; 1339:7162 has no such text node. Shell's own comment (review-client.tsx:97-102) records that the banner is `fixed` at z-[9998] and previously sat on top of the Approve buttons at 1280x720.
recommend: Add the banner to A0 and check the identify submit button against it at 1280x720 the same way the footer was checked.

finding: The 'Signed as {Name}. You are looking at the version sent to you {date}…' sentence is duplicated — once inside the placeholder body box and once in the footer.
evidence: Text dump of 1339:7171 returns the identical string twice; visible in the screenshot at both positions. Code renders it once, in the sticky footer (review-client.tsx:284-288).
recommend: Delete the body copy; keep the footer instance.

finding: The client is asked to approve a revision without being shown what changed. Compare exists only for the agency; the client's only signal is a free-text 'What's new' block the agency may or may not have typed — and that block appears on no board.
evidence: review-client.tsx:309-314 renders the changeSummary block ('What's new') when `data.changeSummary` is present; submitReviewInput carries `changeSummary?: string.max(500)` (packages/shared/schemas/reviews.ts). No compare procedure or view is reachable from /review/[token] — ApprovedCompareView and CompareView are both editor-side (packages/editor/src/editor/panels/version-history/). No Client sign-off board shows the What's-new block, present or absent.
recommend: At minimum board the What's-new block in both states (written / not written). Then decide whether round 2+ should show the client what moved since round 1 — approving blind is the module's weakest moment.

finding: The Review panel's Compare button reaches a loading state and an error state and never a result. The success branch — a side-by-side diff rendered inside a 280px panel — has no board anywhere.
evidence: 156:2's compare hotspot (1720:17537) targets 1717:17246 'Review · compare · loading' (280x260); that frame's only onward edges are back to 156:2 and to 1717:17235 'compare · load-error' (280x300). ReviewTab.tsx:497-520 has three branches under `data-review-state="compare"`: loading, error, and `<ApprovedCompareView approvedPages currentPages … />`. Two are boarded, the third is not. The Compare module's own boards (168:2, 168:26, 168:48, 168:82, 169:2, 169:28) are 1080x776 and are entered from History · Saves (162:2) and Shell (963:4474), never from Review.
recommend: Board ApprovedCompareView at 280px — three modes at that width is the real design problem and nobody has drawn it — or decide Review's Compare opens the 1080px surface and wire 156:2 to 168:2.

finding: Two controls drawn on eleven Review boards cannot be built, and the codebase has already written that down. The '‹ Round 2 of 3 ›' pager has no endpoint behind it, and the button labelled 'Compare with v3' is 'Compare with approved' in code because nothing in the editor knows a version number.
evidence: ReviewTab.tsx:24-28 — 'the round line has no ‹ › pager (no endpoint returns an older round's comments), and Compare is labelled "Compare with approved" rather than the board's "Compare with v3" (nothing here knows a version…)'. Shipped strings: ReviewTab.tsx:419 and :504 both read 'Compare with approved'. Comment has no roundId column — prisma/schema.prisma:471-497, deliberate per review.service.ts:272-277. Board 157:169 records the constraint in its own annotation ('comments carry no round id, contracts §6.4'); the other eleven boards ignore it.
recommend: Relabel to 'Compare with approved' across the module and replace the ‹ › pager with the rounds dropdown that 157:169 already draws — one round navigator, and the one that is buildable.

finding: The two Review compare fragments are off the module's grid in every dimension: 280x260 and 280x300 against the module's uniform 280x812, and parked at x=29127 — roughly 12,000px from every other Review board and adjacent to nothing.
evidence: Frame list: all 13 Review panel boards are 280x812 at x 0-10640, y 26080-27060; 1717:17235 is 280x300 at 29127,740 and 1717:17246 is 280x260 at 29127,1120. Their labels also read 'Compare with approved' while the panel they belong to says 'Compare with v3' (see D-D-11).
recommend: Re-cut both at 280x812 as full panel states and move them next to 156:2. A state of the panel should be the size of the panel.

screen: Review · reply-composer band + foot · revoke + invite
finding: Two of the 23 'screens' are component anatomy in their default, non-error state — a reply composer with nothing wrong with it, and a footer variant. They are parts of 156:2, which already renders both.
evidence: 1705:8704 text: 'Review · Reply to the client… · Replies are internal notes on the thread. · Send'. 1705:8773 text: 'Review · Re-send for review · Invite a client… · Revoke link'. The 156:2 screenshot shows the reply composer and 'Revoke link' already present in the panel. Their sibling error boards (1705:8566 reply-failed, 1705:8636 round-history load-error, 1705:8494 comment-update-failed) are legitimate states and should stay.
recommend: Keep the three error boards as screens; demote these two to component variants, or rename them 'anatomy/…' so the module's screen count stops counting them.

finding: A board whose entire content is a note saying the screen does not exist. It is documentation, and the file already has a Notes section for that.
evidence: 158:213 text in full: 'The Review panel is gone. · This frame documents the ABSENCE — the panel and the 7th rail icon both disappear when the review closes. · Review closed — Sara approved v3 · The Review panel has been removed.' Section 1776:8389 'Notes · captions & annotations' already holds caption/ frames for eleven of the Review boards (161:2-161:12).
recommend: Move it to Notes as a caption. Recorded as a move, not a deletion, per the standing no-delete rule.

finding: Two of the six review states the code can be in have no panel board, and one of them is the outcome the module exists to handle. There is no 'the client asked for changes' Review panel.
evidence: REVIEW_PILL_STATES (packages/shared/schemas/reviews.ts:19-26) = none | pending | opened-not-acted | changes-requested | approved | approved-edited-since. ReviewTab.tsx:1-33 names the 13 boards it implements — open, empty, all-resolved, resolved-expanded, detached-present, older-round, re-send-confirm, re-sending, revoke-confirm, revoked, review-closed, load-error, loading. Neither changes-requested nor opened-not-acted is among them. ReviewBar.tsx:50 keeps the bar ACTIVE for CHANGES_REQUESTED, so the panel is definitely on screen in that state.
recommend: Board 'changes-requested' as a first-class panel state — client's note at the top, the open comments, and the re-send primary — and board 'opened-not-acted' as a variant of 157:221 empty ('Sara opened it 2d ago and has not commented').

finding: The empty state promises a notification that the product does not send: 'Sara has not commented yet. You will be notified.' No review event ever reaches the notification system.
evidence: 157:221 text: 'Sara has not commented yet. · You will be notified.' grep for createNotification in server/services/review.service.ts and server/services/client-review.service.ts returns no match; NOTIFICATION_TYPE_CATEGORY (lib/constants/enums.ts:161-183) has 21 keys and none is review-, comment- or approval-related. The review loop emails only (review.service.ts:502,544,589).
recommend: Either add the review notification types (see D-D-19) or change the copy to name the channel that actually exists — 'We'll email you.'

finding: The agency's own list of every review in flight has no board anywhere in the file. Review is boarded from inside one site's editor panel only, so an agency with twenty sites has no designed way to see who owes them an answer.
evidence: packages/dashboard/app/dashboard/agency/(tabs)/reviews/page.tsx renders <ReviewComments/> (components/reviews/review-comments.tsx), a two-column destination: ReviewQueue (fed by reviews.list, review-queue.tsx:34, with resolve :56 and revoke :45) plus CommentQueue (comments.workspaceList, comment-queue.tsx:27). Its own source comment calls it 'one destination… rendered by the Agency › Reviews tab (D10.4)'. Frame-name search across all 27 sections for /queue|agency|approval|inbox/ returns only Settings Forms inbox boards and captions.
recommend: Board the queue: rows with site + reviewer + state + age, the resolve and revoke actions, and its empty state. It is the agency's half of the loop and the Review section has no screen for it.

finding: Nothing chases a silent client, and nobody is told when a link is about to die. A solo agency can send a review and receive no signal of any kind, ever — because the one email that would tell them filters them out as the sender.
evidence: No match for remind|nudge|remindedAt|followUp anywhere in the review path; ReviewRequest (prisma/schema.prisma:509-554) has no remindedAt and no openedAt; none of the 17 routes under packages/dashboard/app/api/cron/ touches reviews; emails/ holds exactly three review templates (review-invite, review-requested, review-resolved). notifyReviewSubmitted (review.service.ts:568) removes the requester from recipients, returning adminsNotified — which is 0 on a one-seat workspace. Tokens expire silently at +90 days (tokenExpiry, client-review.service.ts:32-33) and board 1339:7200 'F · dead-link · expired' is the first anyone hears of it.
recommend: Board the two states this needs: a 'sent N days ago, not opened — remind Sara' affordance on 157:221, and an 'expires in N days' warning on the round line. The absence is in code as well as design, so this is a product gap, not a drawing gap.

finding: Three of the four notification rows drawn in this module are event types the product cannot emit. The panel's own empty state says 'Client replies and publish results land here' — only publish results do.
evidence: Boards show 'Sara approved Bella Cucina', 'Sara left 3 comments' (165:2, 165:24) and 'Sara commented on Opening hours' (165:71). NOTIFICATION_TYPE_CATEGORY (lib/constants/enums.ts:161-183) declares 21 types; not one is review, comment or approval. Only 6 are ever emitted: MEMBER_JOINED (auth.ts:325), SECURITY_PASSWORD_CHANGED (account.service.ts:30,51), PAYMENT_FAILED (stripe-webhook.service.ts:67), FORM_SUBMISSION_RECEIVED (form-submission.service.ts:60), SITE_PUBLISHED and SITE_PUBLISH_FAILED (api/workers/publish/[jobId]/route.ts:164,219). 'Publish failed — Osteria' is the only real row on the board.
recommend: This is the load-bearing decision for the whole module: either add REVIEW_APPROVED / CHANGES_REQUESTED / COMMENT_ADDED types and call createNotification from review.service.ts, or redraw the panel around the six events that exist. Right now the design's headline content is fiction and the module reads as finished.

finding: The module boards the failure of jumping to a notification's subject but never the success. Every notification carries an actionUrl and no board shows where any of them go — the only onward edges in the module are back to the editor shell.
evidence: All Notifications reactions: 165:2→165:24/165:51/165:71/52:2, 165:24→165:44, 165:44→165:2/453:4051/52:2, 165:51→165:2/52:2, 165:71→165:2/52:2, 453:4051→165:2/165:44/52:2. Every cross-module destination is 52:2 (the editor shell); nothing reaches Review (156:2), Client sign-off, Publish or Pages. Notification.actionUrl exists on every row (prisma/schema.prisma:786). 165:71 exists purely to say 'there is nothing to jump to'.
recommend: Wire and board the successful jump for each event class the product actually emits — publish result → the site, form submission → the submissions inbox — so the panel has a purpose beyond announcing itself.

finding: 165:24 and 165:2 have byte-identical text; the boards differ only in row tint. The frame name already carries the reason ('NO CODE SUBJECT — LoadState is loading|ready|error'), and nothing has acted on it.
evidence: Text dump of both returns 'Notifications · ✕ · TODAY · Sara approved Bella Cucina · 2h · Sara left 3 comments · 4h · YESTERDAY · Publish failed — Osteria · 1d'. NotificationPanel.tsx:98,248-250,267 per the existing frame annotation.
recommend: Merge into 165:2 as a read/unread row variant. Recorded as a merge; no deletion.

finding: A coloured dot is the only thing distinguishing a security alert from a client comment — colour as sole encoding, which this codebase explicitly rejects elsewhere. There is also no visible control for mark-all-read, dismiss, or the Mentions filter, all three of which exist as procedures.
evidence: Screenshot of 165:2: rows carry a green / blue / red dot, no icon and no type label. ApprovedCompareView.tsx:49-55 states the opposite rule for the editor — 'icon + text label + plain-text detail per kind, color never sole encoding'. Procedures with no drawn control: notifications.markAllRead, notifications.delete, notifications.muteType (server/trpc/routers/notifications.ts:22,25,30); the Mentions tab lives in notification-page.tsx. Priority is a real column (prisma/schema.prisma:789) with HIGH_PRIORITY_TYPES in notification.trigger.ts:14-19 and is not expressed at all.
recommend: Give each row an icon plus a short type label, draw the mark-all-read and per-row dismiss affordances, and decide how priority reads. 360x776 with ~660px of it empty has the room.

finding: Users can mute a notification category and choose an email cadence, and there is no board for it in any of the 27 sections — including Settings, which has 45.
evidence: NotificationPref (prisma/schema.prisma:853-862): category, inApp Boolean, email String default 'instant', unique on (userId, category). Procedure notifications.muteType (server/trpc/routers/notifications.ts:30); service muteNotificationType (notification.service.ts:58); UI already built at packages/dashboard/components/settings/notification-prefs.tsx behind /dashboard/settings/notifications. Frame-name search across all sections for /notif|mute|digest/ returns only the six Notifications boards and their captions.
recommend: Board the preferences screen — the eight categories from NOTIFICATION_TYPE_CATEGORY with in-app and email toggles per row. The component exists; the design does not.

finding: The diff itself is not designed. On a 1080x776 board the two compare panes are ~220px tall placeholder rectangles holding one headline each, and the remaining ~500px is empty white. The stepper says '3 of 12 changes' while exactly one change is shown.
evidence: Screenshot of 168:2 — content occupies the top ~140px of 776. Same proportion on 168:26, 168:48, 168:82, 169:2, 169:28. Code renders both sides as full sandboxed iframes with three modes (ApprovedCompareView.tsx:47 `Mode = split|overlay|list`) and five change kinds (approvedCompare.ts:28 `content|style|added|removed|moved`), each with icon + text label + plain-text detail (:49-55). The boards show two kinds ('changed', 'deleted') and no icons.
recommend: Redraw at least side-by-side and list against a realistic page with all five kinds present, and either fill the 776 or cut the frame height to what the design needs.

finding: 'Compare' is one section covering two different code surfaces with different anchors, and the boards do not say which is which. ApprovedCompareView compares against the client's APPROVED snapshot; CompareView compares against another editor version. The boards say 'v3 · approved', which is the first — but Compare's inbound edges come from History · Saves, which is the second.
evidence: Two implementations: packages/editor/src/editor/panels/version-history/ApprovedCompareView.tsx (299 lines, fed by reviews.approvedSnapshot) and CompareView.tsx (234 lines, fed by VersionTimelineManager.compareVersions, versions.ts:147-185). Their labels differ in code: 'Compare with approved' (ReviewTab.tsx:419,504) vs 'Compare with current' (SavesChrome.tsx:137). Inbound edges to 168:2 come from History 162:2 'History · Saves', Shell 963:4474 and Reference 807:6965 — never from Review.
recommend: Split or clearly label the two. As drawn, a reader cannot tell whether Compare belongs to Review or to History, and the answer changes what the left pane is.

finding: Restoring an approved version is the one destructive action in Compare, its confirm board is marked RETIRED for having no producer, and no replacement exists — so restore now has no design at all, in a module whose whole purpose is deciding between two versions.
evidence: 169:60 name: 'Compare · restore-confirm — RETIRED 2026-09-02 (no producer)'. Its copy is complete and correct: 'Restore v3 and lose 12 changes? · Your current work is saved as v4 first — nothing is lost.' No other restore-confirm board exists in Compare or History. Recorded per the brief as context, not as a re-filing of the RETIRED label.
recommend: If restore is a real job, it belongs in History with a producer wired; if it is not, the retirement is complete and nothing more is needed. Flagged so the decision is made rather than inherited.

finding: The orphan-comment trio is the strongest work in the group and needs no change — it names a real failure (a client's comment outliving the element it was pinned to), covers detect, re-attach and keep-as-resolved, and its copy explains the cause ('several orphans usually mean a section was rebuilt rather than edited').
evidence: 184:56/184:70/184:87 at 1440x900, cycled 56→70→87→56, plus an edge into 157:2 'detached-present'. Implemented: editor/canvas/comments/CommentLayer.tsx with commentAnchors.ts (detectOrphans, elementIdFromSelector, pinPosition) and comments.reattach (server/trpc/routers/comments.ts:70, reattachCommentInput requires targetSelector).
recommend: No action. Recorded as the archetype the rest of the module should be measured against.

screen: reviewer reassignment / reopening a closed round
finding: Checked and NOT a gap: reassigning a reviewer and reopening a resolved round are absent from the code by design, so their absence from the design file is correct. Re-submitting after changes-requested IS supported and does have boards.
evidence: No match for reassign|changeReviewer|transferReview in server/; reviewerId is written only by the client's own identifyReviewer (client-review.service.ts:210-213) and resolveReviewByToken (:288), and Reviewer is unique on (siteId, email) (prisma/schema.prisma:572). resolveReview:467-469 and resolveReviewByToken:278-280 both hard-refuse a second resolve, and the client confirm copy says so ('you cannot reopen it', review-client.tsx:387). Re-submit works by opening a NEW round (review.service.ts:53-54,64) and is boarded at 158:2 / 158:57.
recommend: No action. Recorded so a later pass does not file these as missing screens.
